A (universes 0; jacobiMat = ¼[[A,W],A] with scalar (1/4 : ℂ), suDiag = diag(iπk_j), both vocabulary and equal to the blind Kop / milnorA): for any finite index type, ANY integers k_j and ANY complex matrix W, K_A(W)_{jl} = (π²/4)(k_j − k_l)²w_{jl}, plus the commutator formula [diag d, W]_{jl} = (d_j − d_l)w_{jl}. B: the same entry formula for n×n matrices, only for W ∈ 𝔰𝔲(n) and odd k_j with Σk_j = 0. A ⇒ B: rewrite Kop = jacobiMat, milnorA = suDiag, and apply A entrywise. B ⇒ A only vacuously (A re-proved outright, it is a two-line computation): B's restrictions cannot be removed from B itself — with k_j odd, k_j − k_l is always even, so the formula for odd differences is not an instance of B, and the general commutator formula is not in B.
